title: Testware
concept:
**Testware** is the collective term for the work products created during the test process. Testware is delivered alongside the software and must be maintained in the same way: under configuration management, with versions, traceability, and reviews.

Examples of testware include: **test plan**, **test schedule**, **risk register**, **test conditions**, **test cases** (with their inputs, expected results, preconditions, postconditions), **test data**, **test execution schedules**, **test scripts (automated)**, **test logs and incident reports**, **test summary reports**, **test environment setup scripts**, and **test tool configurations**.

Testware needs configuration management for the same reasons code does: changes need to be tracked, versions need to align with the software versions they test (a test case may be valid for v1.0 but invalid for v1.1 after a requirement change), and testware reused across releases needs to be findable.

Reusing testware is a major source of value: a well-organised regression suite gives confidence that previously-fixed defects do not reappear, and avoiding re-derivation of test cases saves significant time on each release.
keyPoints: Testware = all work products produced by the test process: plans, cases, data, scripts, logs, reports, environment configs.
Testware must be under configuration management, with versions aligned to the software it tests.
Reusable testware (regression suites) is one of the most valuable assets a test team builds.

quiz.question: Which of the following is NOT considered testware?
options: The test plan for the next release.
Automated regression scripts in the team's repository.
The source code of the application under test.
The test data files used during system testing.
quiz.explanation: Source code of the AUT is the test object, not testware. Testware is the work products produced for and by the testing activity itself — plans, scripts, data, logs, reports.
